correctness.rationale: A coercive gradient potential yields a positive equilibrium; a strict scaling maximum-ratio argument yields uniqueness. Equilibrium substitution proves a negative-definite quadratic form for the symmetric Jacobian. Summation yields sum (x_i-r_i/2)^2=n q^2/4, and Cauchy--Schwarz plus the constant-vector Rayleigh quotient give alpha<=q with equality exactly when x=(r+q)/2. Equilibrium substitution proves r_i^2-q^2=2d(Lr)_i. Connectedness, strong-mixing eigenvalue separation and continuity prove strict unattainability. A quadratic identity proves the two-value graph eigenvector characterization and three-level impossibility in complete mixing. Actual standalone verification from the package passes 6875 checks. All conclusions are local spectral statements.

The new scoped claim is a universal n-patch RMS spectral ceiling plus exact graph-eigenvector attainability and three growth-level obstruction. Full 2016 Arditi--Bersier--Rohr text addresses mixing and biomass; available 2015 Arditi--Lobry--Sari abstract addresses carrying capacity and its full text was not accessible. value.rationale: The question is the natural fastest *local recovery from perturbation* at the positive population equilibrium, not a routine stability test. The sharp, universal rate bound depends only on measurable intrinsic growth rates and requires no optimization over equilibria; its exact graph criterion identifies when the biological speed limit can be met. The two-rate/three-rate dichotomy and a three-site finite optimal transport example classify a structural barrier, separating optimal mixing from infinite mixing. No downstream theorem beyond this motivated exact graph invariant is required.
